messages:
tim_customer: Hey team — customer reporting intermittent NXDOMAIN when calling our private service endpoint from their Prod VPC. Fails ~30% of requests, works from their dev VPC. Endpoint: payments.internal.redwood.svc.record. Seen since ~0400 UTC.

maria_support: thanks @tim_customer — can you paste a quick `dig` from an instance in the prod VPC (prefer UDP +tcp) and the `resolv.conf`? Also which AZ / subnet the instance is in.

tim_customer: dig output attached (snip):
;; ANSWER SECTION:
payments.internal.redwood.svc.record. 60 IN CNAME payment-us-east-2.lb.redwood.internal.
;; AUTHORITY SECTION:
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 12345

intermittent — sometimes it returns the CNAME (ttl 60) and sometimes NXDOMAIN with no SOA. `resolv.conf` shows 169.254.169.253 as node-local cache, and systemd-resolved pointing to 10.0.2.2

maria_support: corporate note: node-local-cache there could be 169.254.169.253. @eng_jordan can you check if node-local was restarted or if there was a resolver rule change around 04:00?

eng_jordan: looking. I pulled the query logs from our VPC resolver — I see queries for `payments.internal.redwood.svc.record.` going to two upstreams: 10.0.2.2 (route53 resolver) and 172.31.5.6 (forwarder). The forwarder sometimes answers NXDOMAIN after a cached SERVFAIL. Time correlation with a config deploy at 03:58 UTC that updated resolver rules on a subset of accounts.

sre_maya: @eng_jordan can you paste the recorded dns query trace? specifically any SERVFAIL before NXDOMAIN. That pattern usually means a race / negative caching.

eng_jordan: paste snippets:
[03:59:12] query -> forwarder 172.31.5.6: UDP: response=SERVFAIL
[03:59:13] retry -> route53-resolver 10.0.2.2: UDP: response=CNAME
[03:59:45] query -> forwarder 172.31.5.6: UDP: response=NXDOMAIN

So forwarder returns NXDOMAIN after a SERVFAIL, while route53 returns correct CNAME. Clients hitting the forwarder see NXDOMAIN. Node-local or kube-dns sometimes routes to forwarder due to stale rules.

infra_carlos: the forwarder 172.31.5.6 is a managed partner forwarder — they had a brief outage ~03:57 and failover; they may have cached negative responses. If customer VPC health probes hit that forwarder, they get NXDOMAIN.

tim_customer: any quick mitigation? Customer needs the endpoint resolvable for webhooks.

maria_support: short-term: ask them to flush node-local cache and restart kube-dns on a sample node: `kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart daemonset/node-local-dns` and `kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart deployment/coredns` OR run `systemd-resolve --flush-caches` on the host. That will remove the negative cache. Also, make sure the pod's /etc/resolv.conf isn't pinned to the forwarder.

eng_jordan: commands to run from affected instance:
- `dig +tcp payments.internal.redwood.svc.record. @169.254.169.253`
- `dig +tcp payments.internal.redwood.svc.record. @10.0.2.2`
- `tcpdump -i eth0 port 53 -w /tmp/dns.pcap` then reproduce

I can correlate with our resolver logs if they share pcap.

sre_maya: longer-term: we should prevent cross-forwarder negative caching by ensuring consistent order: route53 resolver should be preferred for our private zones and partner forwarders only used for external names. I see a resolver-rule overlap in the VPC: two rules match `*.internal.redwood.svc.` — one forwarding to 10.0.2.2 and a fallback to 172.31.5.6. We need to set rule priority or remove the overlap.

enG_jordan: small correction: AWS resolver rules don't have explicit priority; it's based on association and rule type. Currently both are associated with the VPC which causes non-deterministic selection in rare cases. We should disassociate the forwarding rule for partner forwarder from the prod VPC.

infra_carlos: I'll open a change to disassociate the partner forwarder from prod VPC and keep it on dev. Will also ask partner to clear their cache. ETA 30m.

maria_support: flagged to customer — advising them to flush caches and we will apply the disassociation. Ask if they want a maintenance window.

tim_customer: customer says immediate fix is fine, they're sending a few webhooks to test.

deploy-bot: rollback job started: disassociate-forwarder-prod-vpc (run id 7752) — checks pass.

infra_carlos: done. partner confirmed cache purge. I also removed the association: `aws route53resolver disassociate-resolver-rule --resolver-rule-id rslvr-abcdef123 --vpc-id vpc-0abcde` (ran at 04:32 UTC)

sre_maya: can you run `dig` again and check if any NXDOMAIN remains? Also check negative TTL on the NXDOMAIN responses — if they were cached with low TTL they should expire quickly.

tim_customer: re-run dig from same instance: now consistently gets CNAME. No NXDOMAIN during 10 queries. Webhooks worked. Customer confirms fixed.

maria_support: closing loop with customer and adding notes: root cause = overlapping resolver rules (partner forwarder + route53 resolver) caused occasional selection of forwarder which returned cached SERVFAIL->NXDOMAIN. Fix = disassociate partner forwarder from prod VPC + partner cache purge. Remediation guidance: avoid ambiguous resolver-rule overlaps for private hosted zones; prefer single authoritative route53 resolver for Redwood private zones. Including ask: @eng_jordan can we add an alert if resolver-rule associations overlap across prod VPCs? :eyes:

eng_jordan: will add a policy check in terraform plan and a resolver-rule overlap alert in the console. Thanks team.

maria_support: thanks all — marking resolved. :white_check_mark:
